iconicAnchor.label: Squash-and-stretch animation principles
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: Adobe identifies squash and stretch, anticipation, staging, arcs, and timing as foundational ways to make animated objects feel weighted and alive.

sources.title: 12 Principles of Animation
supports: Squash and stretch, anticipation, staging, arcs, and timing give drawn movement weight, clarity, and expressive life.

sources.title: Stylizing Animation By Example
supports: The paper presents example-driven stylization that preserves expressive drawn appearance with temporal coherence across animated sequences.

bundledReferenceRationale: The repeated bird poses form a clear motion sequence. Arcs, squash-and-stretch, impact marks, expression changes, and consistent character design make motion—not merely sticker styling—the primary lesson. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/motion-sticker/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
